best_for: Music collectors on Windows who need to clean up tags, cover art and file names across thousands of files at once, and Mac users willing to pay for the separate Mac app.
description:
Mp3tag is a music tag editor written by Florian Heidenreich, who has worked on it since 1999 from Dresden, Germany. New versions come out every month or two.

If you fix the same things over and over, you can bundle several steps into an action group and run them on a whole folder with one click. You can pull every embedded album cover out to image files in one go, and set iTunes-specific fields such as media type and TV show details. Beyond the usual formats it handles Opus, DSD (DSF), WavPack, TAK and Matroska audio. Tags and the interface are fully Unicode, so names in any language come through intact, and the interface scales up to 200% on high-resolution screens.

points.title: Free on Windows
points.text: The Windows version costs nothing. Donations are welcome, and the author says not donating does not get you less support or a restricted version.

points.title: Batch tagging for many formats
points.text: It edits tags in MP3, MP4/M4A, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, WMA, WAV, APE and more. You can tag many files at once, rename files from tags or tags from file names, and run search and replace with regular expressions.

points.title: Pulls data from online sources
points.text: Tags and album covers can be looked up from Discogs and MusicBrainz, among other sources. Playlists and exports to HTML, RTF and CSV are also built in.

points.title: Old Windows still welcome
points.text: Version 3.37 supports Windows 7 through 11, with machine-wide 32-bit and 64-bit installers; the 64-bit one also runs on Arm64 PCs. Older releases exist for XP and earlier.

points.title: The Mac app is separate and paid
points.text: Mp3tag for Mac is a different app with its own numbering, 1.15.1 here against 3.37 on Windows. It has a 7-day trial that counts only days you use it, then you buy it directly or from the Mac App Store. It needs macOS 10.14.6 and runs natively on Apple silicon.

points.title: Only the latest version here
points.text: Both the Windows and macOS listings keep only the current release, so a downgrade needs another source.
